title: Sundar Pichai on Google launching Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model yet
content: Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model yet, topping 13 of 18 benchmarks against OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. The model targets coding, legal, finance and cybersecurity work, with a 1 million token output limit. It is rolling out first to cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program, with paid API users and Google AI Ultra subscribers next in line.

title: Wife gets late husband's job, leaves in-laws; HC orders 25% salary for mother-in-law
content: In this case, a widow secured a government job under this provision but later allegedly left her late husband's parents on their own. The Rajasthan High Court explained that a compassionate appointment is intended to provide monetary support to a family struggling to cope with the sudden death of its sole earning member.

title: Man paid $2.48 for old document; a year later, it sold for $477,650
content: While browsing a thrift store in Nashville, Michael Sparks stumbled upon an astonishing find: a rare 1823 copy of the Declaration of Independence, priced at only $2.48. Upon delving into its history, Sparks recognized its immense value and chose to auction it. To his amazement, the document fetched $477,650 at auction, enriching the known collection of surviving copies and transforming Sparks into a local legend.

title: Ohio farmer with $1m medical debt sold land after officials blocked solar lease
content: In Ohio, farmer Wayne Greier's financial struggles intensified when a planned solar project fell through due to local resistance and new rules, leaving his family's renewable energy plans in jeopardy. Compounded by $1 million in medical debt from recent health issues, Greier was forced to offload land and equipment, jeopardizing his farming business. He has emerged as an advocate for farmers' property rights to help protect others from similar hardships.

title: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions
content: Vladimir Putin expressed concerns about current global tensions and the potential for disastrous outcomes from escalating conflicts. He emphasized the importance of preventing the use of weapons of mass destruction in international disputes. Putin highlighted the role of Western technical support in Ukraine's military actions against Russia. He stated that Russia is not planning attacks on European countries but would respond to any aggression.

title: Massachusetts couple wins $310,000 judgment in neighbour tree dispute
content: A Massachusetts couple achieved a remarkable win in their legal battle against their neighbor, successfully advocating for themselves in court. They were awarded $310,000 for damages due to tree destruction and unauthorized encroachments. The ruling by the Massachusetts Appeals Court upheld their victory, emphasizing that self-represented individuals can indeed confront intricate legal issues effectively. This judgment concludes a drawn-out conflict over property rights and associated damages.

title: How Maria Sharapova built a $220 million fortune beyond tennis
content: Sharapova used her tennis success to build a bigger business career after retiring. Her estimated $220 million fortune has been tied to career earnings, global endorsements, Sugarpova and investments in consumer, wellness, fitness and technology companies, allowing the five-time Grand Slam champion to build a financial portfolio outside of professional tennis.

title: Tyreek Hill next team: Vikings and Packers emerge as possible landing spots
content: Tyreek Hill has not been signed by any NFL team, largely because of his recovery timeline. Though he seems ready, he recently expressed his desire to join a cold-weather team. This could mean the Minnesota Vikings, as Justin Jefferson is suffering from an ankle injury. It could also be the Green Bay Packers, since Jayden Reed is out for the season.

title: UK-Iranian man arrested over security incident at US-run military base in England
content: A UK-Iranian dual national was arrested in London over a security incident linked to RAF Fairford. The incident followed the arrest of five British men suspected of preparing a terrorist act. Authorities are investigating potential foreign state involvement, particularly from Iran, which has denied any connection. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has indicated strong signs suggesting Iran's role in the incident.

title: India, Pakistan, Australia in same group for 2027 ODI World Cup
content: India and Pakistan, along with Australia, will be part of Group A in the upcoming 2027 ICC Men's ODI World Cup. The tournament is set to take place in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia, starting on October 2 and concluding on November 21. A total of 14 teams will participate, divided into two groups of six after a preliminary stage.

title: Unimaginable grief: 8 Pune students on school picnic drown at Diveagar beach
content: A picnic at Diveagar beach turned tragic when eight students from Pune drowned after being swept away. They misjudged the sea's depth and current strength, leading to their distress. Local authorities and rescue teams responded promptly to recover all eight bodies. Maharashtra ministers expressed their condolences and sought details regarding the incident. Legal and administrative procedures are currently being conducted at the site of the tragedy.

title: 'Smiling & laughing': India's envoy to UAE meets flydubai hero pilot Smit Machchhar
content: Indian ambassador Deepak Mittal visited Captain Smit Machchhar at the hospital following the stabbing incident. Captain Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot while flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv. After the initial treatment in Saudi Arabia, he was airlifted to Abu Dhabi for further medical care. Passengers and two other pilots helped to restrain the attacker and safely landed the flight.

title: Flydubai incident: Indian pilot stable, co-pilot in custody; Saudi, UAE launch probes
content: On a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, the Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar sustained serious injuries but managed to unlock the cockpit door. Passengers intervened and overpowered the co-pilot, ensuring the safety of everyone aboard. The flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia, where all 174 people landed safely. Investigations by authorities from Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Israel are ongoing.

title: India World Cup 2027 Match schedule: Full fixture list, dates, venues
content: India have been placed in Group A along with Pakistan, Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and Qualifier A. The much-awaited India-Pakistan clash will take place on October 10 in Johannesburg. India will begin their 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against Australia on October 7 in Cape Town.

title: Indian IT sector layoffs: Which jobs are facing pressure & which skills are in demand?
content: AI is not just making some jobs in the Indian IT sector obsolete, it is also forcing firms to adapt their business models as the demand for their traditional services faces disruption. In FY27, hiring is expected to remain subdued, while attrition is increasingly being backfilled selectively rather than one-for-one.

title: Govt limits sugar stock limit to 1,000 quintals ahead of festive season
content: The Centre will implement new stock limits for sugar dealers starting October 15 until November 30. The inventory cap has been set at 1,000 quintals with a 15-day holding period. This decision follows a notable decrease in ex-mill sugar prices and aims to control hoarding during the festive season. Kolkata and Assam have been given slightly higher stock limits due to distribution needs.

title: Iran summons UK envoy after PM Burnham hints Tehran link in Fairford 'terror plot'
content: Iran's foreign ministry expressed its discontent by summoning the British ambassador, following remarks made by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham about Tehran's alleged role in a recent incident at RAF Fairford. Iranian officials rebuffed these claims, suggesting they shifted focus from British military operations against Iran, particularly the US usage of UK bases. Meanwhile, five British men were initially detained over a suspected terror plot but were ultimately released.

title: ICC ODI World Cup 2027 full schedule: Who plays whom, full fixtures, dates and venues
content: India will begin their ICC ODI World Cup 2027 campaign against Australia on October 7 in Cape Town, after the ICC announced the schedule for the tournament on Thursday. India and Pakistan have been placed in the same Group A, setting up another much-awaited clash between the two teams.

title: Iran military kills 6 in Zahedan, accuses armed groups of ties with foreign powers
content: Iranian military forces killed six members of a designated terrorist group in Zahedan on Thursday. Clashes between security forces and armed groups frequently occur in Sistan-Baluchistan province, highlighting ongoing regional tensions. The Iranian revolutionary guards reported finding explosive packages with the detained individuals during their operation. Meanwhile, Tehran is contemplating the United States' response to its recent peace proposal for reviving negotiations.

title: 'Kill me, kill me': Netanyahu reveals words of 'indoctrinated' flydubai co-pilot

Investigative efforts are underway, following a situation where the critically injured pilot managed to alert authorities and enable passengers, alongside off-duty pilots, to subdue the attacker, resulting in an emergency landing.

title: Harekala Hajabba turned one painful moment into a mission to build a village school
content: Harekala Hajabba, despite facing a significant language barrier, pursued a transformative vision for his community through education. Lacking formal schooling, he understood how education could help alleviate poverty. He began his journey by saving profits from orange sales, ultimately earning national acclaim as a recipient of the Padma Shri award. His story serves as a powerful testament to how individual determination can uplift an entire community.

title: Drama! India’s Asian Games medal upgraded: Finished fourth, now bronze
content: Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma from India initially placed fourth in the women's skiff sailing event. They received a bronze medal after the Chinese pair was disqualified for an undisclosed reason. The competition took place at the Kaiyoh Yacht Harbor in Aichi, Japan. Japan finished first with 14 net points, followed by Hong Kong with 18 points. India's final tally allowed them to secure the bronze, making a historic achievement.

title: Gadkari backs IIT tech; waste plastic used in bitumen for NH-44 for first time
content: A pilot test section was laid recently along the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials involved in the pilot said the technology could lower the consumption of conventional bitumen by around 4%, reducing demand for a material that India largely imports to meet its domestic needs.

title: Thomas Stone paid $400 for 442-acre Maryland estate; it became historic site
content: Originally founded by John Barefoot and expanded by Daniel Jenifer, Haberdeventure estate is steeped in history. Thomas Stone bought the estate in 1770, preserving it within his family for 166 years. A significant fire in 1977 led to protective actions and, in 1978, it became the Thomas Stone National Historic Site. Following restorations completed in 1997, it now spans 328 acres, serving as a historical hub for inquisitive visitors.

title: 12 paintings hidden for 50 years head to auction valued near $450 million
content: An exceptional auction is on the horizon for November 18, 2026, showcasing a collection of twelve remarkable impressionist and post-impressionist pieces, valued at almost $500 million. Highlighted artworks include Vincent van Gogh’s 'Châtaigniers en fleurs' and Paul Cézanne’s 'Arlequin,' which have not been publicly available for decades. Sotheby's is optimistic about attracting a global congregation of elite buyers, promising a historic event in the world of art sales.

title: Odisha man left job to build seed bank saving India’s traditional rice varieties

The seed bank contains 1,480 rice landraces collected from various locations and contributed to national conservation efforts. By June 2026, over 8,000 farmers in 13 states received rice seeds through Vrihi's programs. The organization also assists in establishing community seed banks across India.

title: 'Don't want BJP to come': AIMIM leaves door open for alliance ahead of 2027 UP polls

title: Watch: Hero flydubai pilot treated shortly after landing; airlifted to Abu Dhabi

Machchhar’s quick thinking enabled him to unlock the cockpit door, facilitating crew intervention. Passengers stepped in heroically to restrain the co-pilot. Subsequently, Machchhar was airlifted to a medical facility in Dubai as authorities in Saudi Arabia and the UAE begin investigations into this disturbing incident.

title: Dubai-London flight diverted to Frankfurt after passenger’s medical emergency
content:
Flight EK31 was diverted to Frankfurt, where the aircraft landed safely (Photo: Reuters).

An Emirates flight from Dubai to London Heathrow was diverted to Frankfurt after a passenger suffered a medical emergency on board, the airline said. Flight EK31 landed safely in Frankfurt, where the passenger disembarked to receive further medical attention. Emirates said its cabin crew assisted the passenger during the flight and medical support was arranged upon arrival. The flight was expected to resume its journey to London Heathrow at around 6pm local time, the airline said. The diversion came a day after a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia following an alleged cockpit attack, in which one pilot reportedly stabbed the other in an apparent attempt to crash the aircraft.

title: IAF signs Rs 135cr deal with Indian startup for Mirage pilot simulators
content: Threye Interactive, a subsidiary of newSpace Research & Technologies, has signed a Rs 135-crore contract with the Indian Air Force to develop part-task simulators for its Mirage 2000 fighter jets . the company will provide indigenous parts-task combat training simulators specifically designed for the fleet . pilots can work through a difficult sequence, review mistakes and try again without using an actual sequence .
